title: Settings page
blurb: A stock Tailwind settings form, with every section stacked, one Save at the very bottom and a red Delete workspace next to Update, became sectioned forms that show what a change will do before you save it: renaming the workspace URL lists the 23 shared links and 2 embeds it affects and how long the old links redirect.

persona.name: Sam Okafor
persona.goal: Invite a new analyst, change a teammate's role and rename the workspace URL without breaking anything or deleting the wrong thing.

before.verdict: Clean and plausible, like any Tailwind form starter, until you use it. Placeholder-only fields, one Save at the bottom of a five-section form, toggles that are divs, a member table that hides Role and Remove off to the right, and a red Delete workspace beside Update workspace guarded only by "Are you sure?"

after.verdict: Renaming the workspace URL, the riskiest everyday change here, previews its impact live: old and new URL, an availability check, 23 shared links, 2 embeds and a 90-day redirect, and Save stays blocked while the name is taken. Elsewhere a bounced invite offers the likely fix, unsaved changes are counted with a Discard, and usage shows the projection against the alert, not just a bar.

critique.title: Destructive actions guarded by "Are you sure?"
critique.detail: Delete workspace is a red button sitting right beside Update workspace, and it and Remove member both run `confirm('Are you sure?')`. The prompt never says what will be deleted or that it can't be undone.

critique.title: Fields have no labels and no validation
critique.detail: Inputs rely on `placeholder="Full name"`, which disappears once filled; with every field the same gray-300 box, "tidepool-growth" doesn't even say it's the workspace URL. It accepts "Tidepool_Growth" and only fails after the single Save at the bottom, with `alert('Settings saved!')` either way.

critique.title: Toggles and tabs can't be reached by keyboard
critique.detail: Notification toggles are divs with onclick, so Tab skips them. Buttons set `focus:outline-none` with no ring, so only the inputs show focus.

critique.title: Long emails break the member table
critique.detail: Emails are `whitespace-nowrap`, so aleksandra.wisniewska-kowalczyk@… pushes Role, Last active and Remove out of view inside an `overflow-x-auto` box, even on desktop; at 390px only Name is visible. Edit and Remove are 12px text links, and roles are badges you can't change.

critique.title: One long form, one Save, nothing leads
critique.detail: Profile, workspace, members, notifications and billing are identical white panels stacked down one page, all with blue-600 buttons. Save sits at the very bottom, under Billing, and doesn't say which of five sections it saves; Update workspace and Invite act immediately, so it's unclear what Save covers.

critique.title: Fake reassurance in billing
critique.detail: "99.9% Uptime" and "Upgrade Now 🚀" sit where the next invoice amount and usage against the plan limit should be.

changes.before: <input placeholder="Workspace URL"> saved by the one Save at the bottom
changes.after: Impact preview: app.tidepool.example/tidepool-growth → growth-team, "23 shared dashboard links", "2 embedded charts", "Old links redirect for 90 days, until Jan 17, 2027"
changes.why: Sam sees what breaks and what doesn't before renaming, so he can do it without asking engineering.

changes.after: Debounced check: running → "growth belongs to another workspace. Try growth-team"; button reads "Rename and save" and is blocked while taken
changes.why: Collisions are caught as you type, with a usable suggestion.

changes.before: One Save at the bottom of the page → alert('Settings saved!')
changes.after: Per-section "1 unsaved change · Discard", unsaved pip in the section nav, Saving… → "Renamed to app.tidepool.example/growth-team"
changes.why: Sam knows what's pending in each section and can back out of it.

changes.after: Bounced row: "Couldn't deliver. No mailbox at fjordlab.example.se. Did you mean fjordlabs?" + Fix and resend; Dana: "Opened the email Oct 18" + Resend
changes.why: The invite that silently failed is the one Sam needs to see, with the fix in one click.

changes.before: Div toggle rows with 12px gray-500 hints
changes.after: Inline threshold "falls more than [3] points below its 4-week average" + per-row history: "Hasn't fired in 12 weeks"
changes.why: Sam tunes the alert in place and knows whether it's too sensitive.

changes.after: 4,212 of 10,000, projected bar to ~6,900 by Nov 1, tick at the 8,000 alert
changes.why: Answers "will we go over?" rather than only "how much have we used?"

changes.after: <dialog> naming Tidepool Growth, typed-slug confirm that follows a rename
changes.why: The button stays disabled until the current slug matches.

changes.after: Row leaves + toast with Undo; member count and 6-of-10 seat pips update
changes.why: Reversible actions don't need a confirm.

changes.before: <table> with whitespace-nowrap emails in overflow-x-auto; Role and Remove off-screen at 390px
changes.after: Grid rows; under 720px invites stack state, expiry and actions on their own lines
changes.why: No horizontal scroll at 320px, and long emails still fit.

changes.before: .btn { background: #2563eb } on every action; .btn-red Delete workspace beside Update workspace
changes.after: --accent teal for the one primary action per section, red only for the bounce and the danger zone, which moves to its own section at the end; status marks shared with the dashboard
changes.why: Color means state and priority, and the destructive action is no longer one mis-click from a routine one.

tells: Every section an identical white panel
One global Save at the very bottom
Destructive button next to a routine one
